title: openai-compat: tool_choice semantics, schema mapping, and tool message formatting
author: Maya Singh
description:
Motivation: bring Redwood's OpenAI compatibility layer closer to upstream OpenAI function/tool-calling semantics so customers using tool schemas and tool_choice behavior see identical signals when migrating. This PR addresses three customer-facing gaps found during partner testing: 1) tool schema mapping: convert Redwood tool definitions (parameters, types, required/optional, enums) to the OpenAI-compatible JSON Schema shape and back-compatibly accept both shapes on input; 2) tool_choice semantics: add explicit tool_choice field on model responses and expose the chosen tool via the same top-level metadata OpenAI clients expect; 3) tool message formatting: format the tool invocation messages (role/name/content/arguments) to match OpenAI chat/tool payload conventions and ensure streaming emits tool selection and tool output tokens in the same sequence as OpenAI. Summary of changes: - new adapter layer redwood/openai_compat/tool_schema_adapter.go and tests - tool_choice support in runtime/handler and API response envelope - streaming encoder updates to emit tool choice and tool message frames - updated docs/examples in redwood-docs/openai-compat/tool-calling.md - migration shim to accept legacy tool schemas for one release cycle Compatibility notes: this is non-breaking for existing Redwood SDKs; we add an opt-in header "X-OpenAI-Compat: 1" which the API will auto-enable for requests containing OpenAI-style tool schemas. We also add a config flag to Redwood Dedicated/Private to toggle strict mode. Checklist:
- [x] implement schema adapter and round-trip tests
- [x] add tool_choice field in response envelope and wire to runtime
- [x] update streaming encoder to include tool frames
- [x] update SDK examples and docs
- [x] add integration test against openai-compat harness
- [x] e2e perf smoke to ensure no latency regression (>1% token latency)
commits_summary: Initial adapter and tests; add tool_choice to response envelope; wire runtime to set tool_choice; streaming encoder: emit tool frames; update docs and examples; add integration tests and fix flakiness
diff_highlights:
- Added adapter that maps Redwood Tool struct to OpenAI JSON Schema (parameters -> properties, required, types, enum).
- Added 'tool_choice' string and 'tool' object in response envelope.
- Streaming: emit control frames: 'tool_choice' then 'tool_message' chunks; decoder updated to reassemble.
- Docs and examples demonstrating OpenAI tool schema payloads and migration header.

release_notes:
OpenAI compatibility: tool calling improvements
- Adds OpenAI-compatible tool schema mapping (parameters -> JSON Schema)
- Exposes model 'tool_choice' in the top-level response envelope
- Formats tool invocation messages to match OpenAI chat/tool conventions
- Streaming now emits tool frames to ensure client-side decoders can reproduce tool selection and output
Migration: We accept legacy Redwood tool schemas for one release; enable strict OpenAI validation with 'openai_compat.strict' config in Dedicated/Private.
notes_for_ops: Feature flag 'openai_compat.accept_legacy_schemas' defaults to true for one release; ops should flip to false after customers migrate. Dedicated/Private operators can set 'openai_compat.strict=true' to enforce exact schema shape. No additional infra required.
backwards_compatibility: Opt-in via header X-OpenAI-Compat: 1 or via feature flag. Legacy tool schemas accepted during migration window. SDK examples updated to show new response shape. No breaking change expected for existing Redwood clients.
performance_impact: Perf smoke showed +0.6% median token latency due to additional streaming frame assembly; considered acceptable. Added encoder optimizations to limit allocations.
security_considerations: Adapter validates incoming JSON Schema shape and rejects unrecognized types. Tool arguments are still passed to configured tool runners under existing RBAC controls. No new secrets introduced.
qa_notes: Run the openai_compat integration test against both strict and legacy modes. Verify streaming client receives 'tool_choice' frame before tool_message frames and that SDK decoders map to tool invocation APIs. Check logs for migration shim warnings.
